title: Student identity linked to submission data
description: The student's identity (via login credentials and student ID) can be linked to their assignment submission data (work file, course, timestamp), potentially enabling profiling or tracking of student behavior across submissions.
assumptions: The system stores and processes both identity and submission data in a way that allows correlation.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: Student's assignment submissions (work file, student ID, course, timestamp) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, insider threats, or improper access controls.
assumptions: The system has access controls that may be bypassed or misconfigured.

title: Unauthorized submission usurpation
description: An attacker could usurp the student's identity to submit assignments on their behalf, potentially through credential theft, session hijacking, or authentication bypass.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to credential compromise or session attacks.

title: Assignment data alteration
description: The submitted assignment data (work file, student ID, course, timestamp) could be altered by an attacker with system access, compromising data integrity and potentially affecting grading accuracy.
assumptions: The system may lack adequate integrity controls or audit logging for submitted data.

title: Transmission of Student Identifiers to Grading Service
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) transmits student id, course, file reference, and requesting role to the Assignment & Grading Service (P2). This flow carries unique identifiers that can link data to specific students, creating privacy risks if the receiving system is not properly secured or if data is exposed.
assumptions: Student identifiers are transmitted in clear or insufficiently protected form during the process-to-process flow.
uncertainty_note: Using I.2.1.1 from context as it directly addresses identifier transmission in Process→Process flows.

title: Processing of Identified Student Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) receives and processes identified data including student id, course, and file reference. This processing of personally identifiable information creates privacy exposure if the service lacks appropriate access controls or if data is retained longer than necessary.
assumptions: P2 processes the received data for grading and assignment management purposes.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 from context describes processing of identified data, applicable to P2's role as data receiver and processor.

title: Non-repudiation of Submission and Grading Actions
description: The flow involves submission and grading requests where students and instructors may need to deny or confirm their involvement. Without proper audit trails or cryptographic evidence, parties may be unable to deny claims about their actions (e.g., whether a student submitted an assignment or an instructor graded it).
assumptions: The system does not implement robust non-repudiation mechanisms for tracking submission and grading actions.
uncertainty_note: Nr threat type based on context [4] about non-repudiation in privacy contexts; tree node Nr.1.1 inferred as standard non-repudiation node for action attribution.

title: Unintended Data Disclosure via Assignment Storage
description: The Assignment & Grading Service stores assignment files containing student identifiers, course information, and submission timestamps. This creates a data disclosure risk where personal data is transferred to the data store, potentially exposing student information to unauthorized access or unintended third parties.
assumptions: The data store may have access controls that are not properly enforced, or the data could be accessed by personnel beyond those with legitimate need-to-know.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 based on context [5] regarding data disclosure across boundaries

title: Linkability of Assignment Data to Student Identity
description: The stored assignment data includes student IDs and course information, enabling potential linking of assignment submissions to specific students across different courses or time periods. This could allow profiling or tracking of student behavior.
assumptions: Multiple data sources or systems may contain overlapping student information that could be correlated.
uncertainty_note: Linkability depends on whether other systems contain complementary data

title: Data Integrity Risk for Stored Assignments
description: Assignment files and metadata stored in the Assignment Store could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted, potentially affecting grading accuracy or creating false records of student submissions.
assumptions: The data store may lack adequate integrity controls, encryption, or audit logging mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Integrity risks depend on the security controls implemented at the data store

title: Processing of identified student submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes student submission data that contains identifiable information (student names, IDs, and potentially personal details). When teachers review submissions, the system processes this identified data, creating privacy risks for students whose data is being accessed.
assumptions: Student submissions contain personally identifiable information that is processed during the review workflow.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: The system may disclose student submission data to teachers who are not properly authorized to access it, or to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities. This could occur if access controls are not properly enforced during the submission review process.
assumptions: Access controls may not be properly implemented or enforced for student data access.

title: Teacher identity usurpation during login
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate a teacher during the login process to the Grades Portal Web App, gaining unauthorized access to student submission data. This is a critical threat given the sensitive nature of the data being accessed.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to credential theft or session hijacking.

title: Linkability of student submissions across multiple submissions
description: Teacher can link student submissions across different assignments or time periods, potentially creating a comprehensive profile of student behavior and performance patterns.
assumptions: Teacher has access to historical submission data and can correlate submissions by student identity.

title: Identification of students through submission display
description: Student names are displayed alongside work content, enabling identification of students who have submitted work. This could expose student identity to unauthorized parties if the teacher account is compromised.
assumptions: Student names are included in the displayed data and teacher has access to the portal.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student work content
description: Student work content (assignments, essays, projects) is disclosed to the teacher. If teacher credentials are compromised or if the teacher shares data with unauthorized third parties, student intellectual property and personal information could be exposed.
assumptions: Teacher has legitimate access but may share data with others or credentials may be compromised.

title: Usurpation of teacher identity
description: An unauthorized actor could impersonate the teacher to access student submissions, potentially viewing or downloading student work without proper authorization.
assumptions: Teacher authentication is not sufficiently secure or teacher identity can be spoofed.

title: Student data linkability across system flows
description: Student identifiers recorded in this flow could be linked to other student data flows (e.g., enrollment, attendance, other grades), creating a comprehensive student profile that exceeds the scope of this single data flow.
assumptions: System contains multiple data flows involving student identifiers
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 chosen based on standard LINDDUN Pro methodology for linkability threats at source position

title: Student and grader identification from recorded data
description: The student id and grader id fields directly identify individuals. Student identities could be inferred from grade records, and teacher identities are explicitly recorded as grader ids.
assumptions: Student and teacher identities are not anonymized in the system
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 chosen based on standard LINDDUN Pro methodology for identification threats at source position

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades and feedback
description: Written feedback and grades could be disclosed to unauthorized parties (e.g., other students, unauthorized personnel) through improper access controls or data leakage in the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Access controls may not be properly implemented or enforced
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 chosen based on standard LINDDUN Pro methodology for disclosure threats at source position

title: Teacher identity usurpation for grade recording
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate a teacher to record grades and feedback, leading to unauthorized grade manipulation and feedback injection.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may not be robust enough to prevent identity spoofing
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 chosen based on standard LINDDUN Pro methodology for usurpation threats at source position

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: The grading service writing to the Grade Records Database could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties, exposing sensitive student grades and personal information.
assumptions: Database access controls are not properly implemented or are bypassed

title: Student and Grader Identification
description: The grade records contain student id and grader id, which could be used to identify specific individuals and link their academic performance to their identity.
assumptions: Student and grader identifiers are not properly anonymized or protected

title: Grade Record Tampering
description: Grade records written by the grading service could be altered or corrupted during storage, leading to inaccurate academic records and potential grade manipulation.
assumptions: No integrity controls or audit trails exist for grade records

title: Grader Identity Impersonation
description: An unauthorized actor could impersonate a grader and write fraudulent grade records to the database, compromising the integrity of the grading process.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms for the grading service are weak or bypassed

title: Insecure Data Storage of Grade Records
description: The Grade Records Database may store sensitive student and grader information without adequate encryption or access controls, leading to potential data breaches.
assumptions: Database security measures are insufficient for the sensitivity of stored data

title: Regulatory Compliance Violation
description: Storage of student grades and personal identifiers in the database may violate privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) if data protection measures are inadequate.
assumptions: Data handling does not meet applicable privacy law requirements

title: Processing of identified student grades and feedback
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes the student's grades and feedback, which are inherently identifying personal data. Processing identified data creates privacy risks as it enables the system to maintain records that can be linked to the specific student.
assumptions: The system stores and processes grades and feedback that can be associated with the student's identity.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades
description: Student grades and feedback may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data breaches, or insecure transmission channels. Grades are sensitive academic information that should be protected.
assumptions: The system may have vulnerabilities in access control or data transmission that could expose grades to unauthorized users.

title: Unauthorized access to student grades
description: An unauthorized user could potentially impersonate the student or exploit authentication weaknesses to access the student's grades and feedback without proper authorization.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may have vulnerabilities or the student's credentials could be compromised.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades
description: Student grades and teacher feedback displayed by the portal could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through vulnerabilities, misconfiguration, or insider threats.
assumptions: Grades are sensitive personal data that should only be accessible to the student and authorized personnel.

title: Unauthorized access to student grades
description: An attacker could gain unauthorized access to the student's grades and feedback through authentication bypass, session hijacking, or privilege escalation.
assumptions: The portal has authentication mechanisms that could potentially be compromised.

title: Linkability of grades to student identity
description: Student grades could be linked to other personal information or external data sources, potentially enabling profiling or correlation attacks.
assumptions: Grades are displayed in a context where they could be correlated with other identifiable information.

title: Identifiability of student from grades
description: The student could be identified from their grades and feedback, especially if displayed in a public or semi-public context.
assumptions: Grades may contain unique patterns or be displayed in contexts where the student is identifiable.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's grades to unauthorized parties
description: The Grades Portal Web App may disclose a child's grades to unauthorized parties if authentication/authorization controls are insufficient. Since the flow involves sensitive educational data, improper access control could lead to grade leakage to non-parent entities.
assumptions: System has access control vulnerabilities or misconfigured permissions
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a standard disclosure node; confidence in exact node selection is moderate.

title: Linkability between parent identity and child's grades
description: The system may link the parent's identity to their child's grades in a way that creates privacy risks. If the system doesn't properly separate or anonymize this linkage, it could enable profiling or tracking of the parent-child relationship beyond intended purposes.
assumptions: System stores parent-child relationship data that could be exploited for profiling
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a standard linkability node; confidence in exact node selection is moderate.

title: Parent account usurpation/impersonation
description: An attacker may usurp the parent's account to access their child's grades. Since the flow starts with parent login, if authentication is weak or compromised, unauthorized access to sensitive grade information could occur.
assumptions: Authentication mechanism has vulnerabilities or parent credentials are compromised
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a standard usurpation node; confidence in exact node selection is moderate.

title: Linkability of child's academic data to other profiles
description: Parent may link the displayed grades, feedback, and submission history to other information about the child (e.g., personal details, other services), creating a comprehensive profile that could be misused.
assumptions: Parent has access to other data sources about the child; data displayed contains identifiers that enable linking.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a reasonable fit for linkability concerns in Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades and feedback data
description: Grades, feedback, and submission history may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data logging mechanisms.
assumptions: System has access controls; data is logged or transmitted; parent account may be compromised.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a standard disclosure node for Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Usurpation of parent identity to access child's academic data
description: An unauthorized actor may usurp the parent's identity to access the child's grades, feedback, and submission history, potentially through credential theft or session hijacking.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms exist; parent credentials may be compromised; session management may be vulnerable.
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 is appropriate for identity usurpation threats in Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Excessive data sharing beyond necessity
description: The system may share more detailed academic information (e.g., full submission history, detailed feedback) than necessary for the parent's legitimate oversight role, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Data minimization policies exist; system may share comprehensive data; parent may not need all details.
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 fits data minimization concerns for Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Unauthorized Account Creation/Modification
description: School Administrator (EE4) could create, modify, or disable accounts and parent-child links without proper authorization or authentication controls, potentially granting access to unauthorized individuals or altering relationships maliciously.
assumptions: Administrator privileges are not properly bounded or authenticated

title: Sensitive PII Disclosure via Account Management
description: Administrator handling names, emails, roles, and relationships could inadvertently or maliciously disclose sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or data exposure during account operations.
assumptions: Data access controls are insufficient or logging is inadequate

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Account Actions
description: Administrator actions (creating, modifying, disabling accounts and parent-child links) may lack proper audit trails or cryptographic signing, allowing the administrator to deny performing specific actions that affect student/parent data integrity.
assumptions: No comprehensive audit logging or digital signatures for administrative actions

title: Data Integrity Compromise in Account/Relationship Data
description: Administrator could maliciously or accidentally corrupt, alter, or delete account information and parent-child relationship data without proper integrity checks, leading to incorrect or fraudulent records.
assumptions: No data integrity validation or tamper detection mechanisms

title: Administrator Identity Exposure
description: Administrator's identity or role information could be exposed through the Grades Portal Web App interface or logs, potentially revealing organizational structure or access patterns to unauthorized observers.
assumptions: Interface or logging systems expose administrative identity information

title: Identification of Students and Family Members via Account Records
description: The grading service writes account records containing parent-child relationship links to the account directory. This could allow identification of students and their family members through the stored relationships, potentially exposing sensitive family structure information.
assumptions: Account records contain identifiable information about students and their family relationships

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Account Records
description: The grading service writes account records to the account directory. If the data store is not properly secured, sensitive student and family information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the write operation or through subsequent access.
assumptions: The account directory may be accessible to unauthorized entities

title: Unauthorized Modification of Account Records
description: The grading service writes account records and parent-child relationship links to the account directory. Malicious or compromised actors could modify these records, potentially altering student-family relationships or account information.
assumptions: The write operation may not have adequate access controls

title: Linkability of Account Records Across Contexts
description: The account directory stores account records with parent-child relationship links. These records could be linked with other data sources (e.g., academic records, financial data) to create comprehensive profiles of students and their families.
assumptions: The account directory data may be accessible or correlatable with other data sources

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to external cloud hosting provider EE5. This represents an explicit disclosure of personal data across organizational boundary.
assumptions: The cloud provider has access to all student PII including grades and account information

title: Linkability of Student Records Across Systems
description: Account directory and grade records transferred to cloud provider could be linked to identify specific students, potentially enabling cross-referencing with other data sources.
assumptions: Cloud provider may have access to additional data that could be correlated with transferred records
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 inferred from standard LINDDUN methodology for linkability threats

title: Identifiability of Students Through Transferred Data
description: Account directory and grade records contain personally identifiable information that could directly identify students even without additional context.
assumptions: Student names, IDs, and grades are included in the transferred data
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 inferred from standard LINDDUN methodology for identifiability threats

title: Unauthorized Access to Transferred Student Data
description: Data transferred to cloud provider EE5 may be accessible to unauthorized personnel or systems within the provider's infrastructure.
assumptions: Cloud provider has multiple access points and personnel with varying access levels
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 inferred from standard LINDDUN methodology for usurpation threats

title: Linkability of Grade Records to Student Identity
description: Grade records in the database can be linked to specific student identities through student IDs or other identifiers, enabling correlation with other data sources.
assumptions: Student identifiers are present in the grade records and can be correlated with external data.

title: Identification of Students from Grade Records
description: Grade records contain personally identifiable information that can be used to identify individual students, potentially exposing sensitive academic performance data.
assumptions: Grade records include student identifiers that can be used for identification purposes.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grade Information
description: Grade records may be accessed by unauthorized parties through vulnerabilities in the grading service or improper access controls, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Access controls on the grading service may be insufficient or improperly configured.

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations for Grade Data
description: The grading service may fail to comply with privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, FERPA) when processing grade records, leading to legal and reputational risks.
assumptions: The system must comply with applicable privacy regulations for educational data.
